proposal.title: Proposal 5: new, true, checkable mathematics on one machine (2026-10-27)
proposal.companion_reading_log: docs/studies/MATH_SCOUT_2026-10-27.md (19 sources opened, 'seen but not read' list)

user_request: continue finding more real mathematics breakthroughs (verbatim from the proposal)
reading_of_request: We never claim breakthroughs. The aim is new, true, checkable mathematical statements, found by a disciplined, preregistered search with positive and negative controls, audited independently, with negative results published. Every item is small; most close a finite case that someone else has explicitly left open.
method: Elenchus tiers. A = kernel-checked Lean through anse/formal/lean_runner.py, axioms limited to {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}, no sorry, statement locked, leanchecker replay. L = literature pinned to a page. C = human or AI argument, exhaustive enumeration with certified decision rule, or ball arithmetic not replayed in Lean. X = floating point. Tier C enumerations are not Lean proofs; only single certificates (witnesses, coverings, counterexamples) are promoted to Tier A, only through lean_runner.py with a kernel replay.

scales.prior_p: probability that a NEW statement survives its gate within the time box; document says range 0.05 to 0.4, deliberately sceptical
scales.value_v: 1-5: how much a correct result would matter to the people who posed the question
scales.feasibility_f: 0-1: chance we can run the method on this machine at the stated cost
scales.score: p x v x f; all three numbers are our estimates, not measurements

global_rules: Claims are written before the test: each item needs its own preregistration (statement, controls, kill criterion and priors hashed before the first run) before it starts; this proposal itself is not a preregistration.
Every positive and negative control runs and is reported BEFORE any headline number. A failing gate is reported, not hidden.
Producer != verifier: independent audit by Opus, never cheaper than the producer; LR-IND's implementer must not read the S-T repository.
Negative results and null boxes are published with the same care.

No 'breakthrough': each result is a finite case, a bound, an independent check, or a null box, and is said that way in the title. Upper bounds on gamma_sh are not exact values; a computational range is not an answer to a 'for all n' question; an independent re-run is not a new theorem.
Same-day arXiv re-search of the exact case before any item is written up or published (the lonely runner area moves weekly).

Read vs not read: a source is read only if opened in the session (alphaXiv PDF page text or local file); search snippets or references inside other papers are 'not read' and nothing load-bearing rests on them.
Each elementary-attack pass (10-15 minutes of trying for an elementary resolution) must be repeated in each item's own preregistration.

Public data only; no third-party full texts; the repository is PUBLIC, so no third-party full texts, private-repository summaries or dataset files are committed (sha256 and licences recorded instead).
Lean verification only through anse/formal/lean_runner.py; never `import Mathlib` (LL section 3); Lean 4.34.1 pinned, partial Mathlib.
No simulated agents. A stage that cannot run reports BLOCKED.
Each passing item gets a short paper (statement, certificate, controls, code with sha256); independent AI audit before any Zenodo DOI.
The LR-Q84 elementary answer is a remark for the author, not a result of this programme; it will not be counted or titled as a discovery. Do not publish it.

items.title: The shifted lonely runner conjecture fails for every n with 18 <= n <= 94, so it fails for every n >= 5
items.statement: For every n with 18 <= n <= 94 there are distinct positive integers v_1, ..., v_n and shifts s in (Q/Z)^n such that max_t min_i ||s_i + v_i t|| < 1/(n+1). Equivalently, Gamma(n) < 1/(n+1) in Zhang's notation.

items.verifiable_core: For each n, a certificate (v, s, delta = 1/(n+1)). Check: the open bad arcs {t : ||s_i + v_i t|| < delta} cover R/Z, so the continuous min_i ||.|| is < delta everywhere and its maximum is < delta. All endpoints (k +- delta - s_i)/v_i are rational; scale by a common denominator and check the covering with integers. Lean `decide` over at most sum v_i ~ n^2/2 <= 4,500 integer intervals at n = 94 on the pinned stack. Two independent checkers: Python fractions and a C integer checker.
items.tier: A feasible per n (Lean decide, optional, later); Tier C until replayed
method: (i) Port the exact gamma(v;s) evaluator, written by us; Criado's verify_solution.py (not read) serves only as a cross-check.

(ii) For v = [n], search over s: seed with structured s (periodic patterns extrapolated from exact optima at n <= 15; the s for n = 5 is printed in the paper); local search or LP over fixed combinatorics (for a fixed assignment of runners to arcs, min delta is a linear program in (s, delta); scipy HiGHS solves it; round to rationals and re-check exactly).
(iii) If [n] fails, search for a uniform rule in Poliakova's sense with L <= 38, or for modified velocity sets.
(iv) Chain: one vector with gamma_sh <= 1/(m+1+k) covers sizes m+1,...,m+k after adding runners; strictness at the last step checked on the explicit vector, not assumed.
No lower bound on gamma_sh is attempted (hard direction).
positive_controls: Certify < 1/(n+1) for [n], n = 5..17, using our own s (Blanco et al. report all of these as counterexamples)
negative_controls: s = 0 for [n] gives exactly 1/(n+1); it must NOT certify strict <, because arcs are open and tangencies matter
Perturbing one shift by 1/(10*sum v) in a certified case must break the covering
Unshifted LRC holds up to 14 speeds (Allikvere, arXiv 2609.02604, LRC(14), i.e. fifteen runners; Tier L), so no s = 0 instance with <= 14 distinct speeds may ever certify
items.kill_criterion: After 30 core-hours of search, stop and report the certified sub-range, e.g. 'n in [18, N] closed'. Any certificate that fails either independent checker kills that n until the bug is found.
items.cost: about 10-30 core-hours of search, under 1 core-hour of checking, about 20-80 core-hours of Lean replay on the Lean lane (optional, later)
items.prior_note: 0.35 for the full range; about 0.6 for a non-empty sub-range [18, N]
items.novelty_check: alphaXiv sweep (recency) for 'shifted lonely runner conjecture' returned nothing after 2609.23952 except Zhang v3; Zhang v3 (2026-10-18) calls the range open. WebSearch for the range returned only the same papers. Scoop risk is real (groups active, Criado's code public). Before publishing, re-search arXiv the same day.

says nothing about the unshifted LRC
gives no exact Gamma(n), only upper bounds
velocities must be distinct positive integers; the trivial counterexample with repeated velocities must not be used

items.title: Zhang's Question 8.4: deletion values of [n-1] (REMARK ONLY, not a paper)
items.statement: Is LR([n-1] \ {r}) > 1/(n-1) for all n >= 5 and all r <= n-2, where LR(V) = max_t min_{v in V} ||vt||?

items.status: Tier C until audited (elementary argument found during scouting, checked by hand once)

scouting_argument.proof: Take t = 1/r. For 1 <= v < r: ||v/r|| = min(v, r-v)/r >= 1/r. For r < v <= n-1: since 2r >= n, 1 < v/r < 2, so ||v/r|| = min(v-r, 2r-v)/r >= 1/r, because v-r >= 1 and 2r-v >= 2r-(n-1) >= 1. This is the time used in Zhang's Lemma 5.3.
scouting_argument.remaining_finite_set: Corollary 2.10 covers r <= n-2-2 sqrt(n); a gap remains only when n-2-2 sqrt(n) < (n-1)/2, i.e. n-3 < 4 sqrt(n), i.e. n <= 21 (at n = 21 only r = 10 is left; at n = 22, 19 > 4 sqrt(22) ~ 18.76). In that gap r <= (n-1)/2, so Liu's exact formula LR = 2/D_r applies, D_r the least integer >= n+r coprime to r (as quoted by Zhang); reduces to D_r <= 2n-3 for finitely many (n, r): a few dozen pairs, by hand or a one-minute script plus an exact ML scan as independent second check.

items.verifiable_core: Tier X screening with float eigenvalues, then exact re-check of any near-tie or violation (characteristic polynomial via flint, Sturm sequences). A refuting graph is Tier A-checkable for algebraic invariants; Tier C if the invariant needs a numeric eigenvalue bound.
items.tier: X screening; A or C for a refutation
method: own `nauty-geng -c 11` stream, 1,006,700,565 graphs, run in res/mod parts (C1b's code is not modified, because C1b is preregistered)
numpy eigenvalues of A, L, Q and D plus needed invariants (harmonic, temperatures, gravity per the pinned definitions)
flag anything within 1e-6 of violating and re-check it exactly
positive_controls: re-refute already-refuted Graffiti 29 (7 vertices), 166 and 711 (5 vertices)
negative_controls: a known theorem, e.g. lambda_1 >= average degree, must never fire
items.kill_criterion: The definitions cannot be pinned from a primary source, or the run exceeds 20 core-hours.
items.cost: about 10-20 core-hours (geng alone takes core-hours plus eigenvalue cost)
items.novelty_check: Roucairol-Cazenave 2024 is the latest systematic attempt found. AutoGraphForge (arXiv 2609.03478) seen only as a title, not read; must be read before starting. Their searches are heuristic (50 or 100 vertices); most Graffiti conjectures were checked by the authors on small-graph databases, so the prior is low.
over_claim_risks: a refutation under a misread definition is worthless; report the definition source next to every result
'No counterexample on <= 11 vertices' is weak evidence and must be worded that way

items.verifiable_core: A kernel replay (Tier A) of the published certificates on our pinned Lean 4.34.1 stack after porting their Lean development. An independent check, not a new statement. We hold no SDP machinery to regenerate certificates, only to replay them. Certificate size not stated.
method: read their repository
run their Python checkers
port the s in {0,1} Lean development first as a control, then attempt the all-s certificates
positive_controls: their s = 0 and s = 1 theorems replay under our pin with axioms in the whitelist
negative_controls: a tampered certificate entry must be rejected
items.kill_criterion: The s in {0,1} port is not achieved within 40 core-hours, or the all-s certificate size makes the replay exceed 200 core-hours.
items.cost: 40-200+ core-hours, unknown until the repository is read
items.novelty_check: The paper (2026-09-18) states the authors' own plan to do this (high scoop risk). Before starting, check their repository for a newer Lean release.
over_claim_risks: a replay of someone else's proof: never call it ours, never call it new
